mechanism: Proposed port of the 'sticky policy deadline' from the Polyphony ARC agent (Ruiyang Yu et al., Qwen3.6-27B via vLLM) onto our ARC-AGI-3 vehicle. Polyphony abandons uncertified world-model-building for direct play at a fixed fraction (0.55) of the per-game wall-clock. Its stated rationale: 'the likeliest failure of this arm is not a bad policy, it is an elegant policy and zero actions played'. It was proposed here as an engineered answer to our strongest campaign finding - that the per-game decision budget is binding (675/675 game-runs die on the 7920s wall at ~17 turns against a designed 132).
summary: REFUTED ON FIREABILITY BEFORE ANY BUILD, at a cost of one ten-minute measurement over artifacts already on disk. Level-completion times were reconstructed by indexing cumulative actions_per_level into history[] and normalising wallclock_seconds by each run's OWN final wallclock. On the certified baseline vehicle the arm would ship on, 39.3% of all level completions (11/28) and 47.1% of last-level completions (8/17) arrive AFTER the 0.55 mark; pooled over 100 standard-budget game-runs it is 31.7% (33/104). The back 45% of the clock is not slack - it is where roughly a third to a half of our scoring happens - so a deadline there cuts into live scoring rather than reclaiming waste. Separately, the failure mode the deadline exists to prevent does not describe our system at all: our agent plays 2081 actions per 25-game run, so we have a throughput problem, not a paralysis problem, and those call for opposite interventions.
lesson: Borrow a design point only after checking that the failure it prevents is a failure YOU actually have. Polyphony's deadline is a sound answer to paralysis ('elegant policy, zero actions played'); our agent's pathology is the opposite, and importing the remedy would have cut into the back half of the clock where 30-40% of our level completions occur. The general rule: an intervention's rationale travels only with the failure mode it was written against, so restate the source system's failure mode in your own measurements before porting its fix. Corollary on cost discipline: the killing measurement here was computable from artifacts already on disk, so the arm cost ten minutes instead of a GPU slot - always ask what single number would refute the arm, and whether it is already sitting in your retained data.
why_informative: This produces a reusable prior that outlives the rejected arm: on this benchmark and harness our level completions are distributed with a median at 0.31 of the per-game clock and a long tail past 0.85, so any future proposal to truncate, re-phase or re-budget the back half of the game clock must clear that distribution first. It also complements a previously established arithmetic result - that efficiency-family interventions are capped at roughly +0.06 leaderboard points by the score formula - with the empirical half: the back half of the clock is not recoverable waste. And it records a structural mismatch worth knowing before anyone else ports this: Polyphony's deadline switches between two PHASES (uncertified model-building, then direct play) whereas our vehicle plays directly throughout and has no phase boundary to cut, so porting it would have required inventing the boundary first - a different arm than the one whose rationale was being borrowed.

measured.source_system_published_score: Polyphony 19.8% on the ARC Prize community board, against Tycho 100.0% / Retrodict 99.9% / NOOA 85.1% - i.e. a well-argued design from a mid-table system, not a winner

robustness: Instrument audited before the numbers were trusted: wallclock_seconds verified MONOTONIC in all 125 game-runs (0 non-monotonic series). An apparent 2.24x outlier resolved as the 3x-budget arm (final wallclock 23796s = 3 x 7920), correct by construction. Re-normalising per-run rather than against a global 7920s constant moved the headline by 1.5pp (30.2% vs 29.5%), so the finding is not a denominator artefact. The per-game wall is soft: 25/125 runs exceeded 8400s. Reported separately for the baseline vehicle alone, the standard-budget pool, and the full pool; the baseline-alone number is the STRONGEST against the arm, which is the conservative direction since that is the vehicle the arm would have shipped on.
sealed_reading_rule: Standing campaign rule: verify a treatment CAN FIRE on your own rail, measured on retained artifacts, BEFORE building it. Pre-registered kill: if a 0.55 deadline would change behaviour on almost no games, or would sit on top of a material share of actual scoring, report and STOP without building. It sits on top of 39.3% of baseline-vehicle completions. STOPPED. No build, no gate, no slot, no submission.
